mainTopic: Does a קל וחומר override the rule that something does not affect what is not its own kind? The גמרא tests this using the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about a divided oven, and applies it to a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין.
overview: This amud finishes the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about an earthenware oven divided by boards. The רבנן reject רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from טומאת מת. The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר also accepts the rule that something does not affect what is not its kind, but his קל וחומר overrides it. That raises a challenge: a קל וחומר should then make a חטאת slaughtered for חולין פסול. The answer is that רב's ruling comes from a פסוק, ״וְלֹא יְחַלְּלוּ״, and a פסוק beats a קל וחומר. The גמרא then asks why the word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ does not block רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר, and answers that he needs it for food sealed in clay. Next, רב יוסף בר אמי points out that two rulings of רב, one about changing the offering and one about changing the owner, seem to clash. He resolves them with two different פסוקים. Finally, רב חביבא sets רב's owner ruling against the ברייתא of ״תוך תוכו״. He answers that the four mentions of ״תוך״ in the פסוק each teach their own law, so the כלי שטף rule applies only to clay vessels.

steps.title: The רבנן reject רבי אליעזר's comparison to a מת
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר. A partition helps with טומאת מת only because that טומאה spreads through a tent, and tents can be divided. Earthenware vessels are not divided that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a partition protects against a corpse, which is severe, that is because corpse טומאה works through tents, and tents can be divided. Should it then protect inside an earthenware vessel, which is mild, when vessels are not divided the way tents are?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the רבנן's reply to רבי אליעזר in the case of the divided oven. They knock down his קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר argued: if a partition protects in the severe case of a מת, it should surely protect in the milder case of a כלי חרס. The רבנן point to a special feature of טומאת מת: it works through אהל, and a tent can be split by a partition. A כלי חרס has no such feature, so the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: protected (kept something from becoming טמא)
a dead body, the most severe source of טומאה
tents or roofs; טומאת מת spreads to whatever is under the same roof
an earthenware vessel, which becomes טמא through its inside airspace
severe / mild, the two sides of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: This is the רבנן talking, not רבי אליעזר. They repeat his words 'if it protects against a corpse' only to turn his argument around.

phrases.english: If [a partition] protected against a corpse, which is severe,
that is because it is divided in tents,
phrases.notes: He means that טומאת מת spreads by tent, and a tent can be split into parts by a partition.

phrases.english: should it protect in an earthenware vessel, which is mild,
where they are not divided as tents are?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הִצִּיל בְּמֵת חָמוּר שֶׁכֵּן חֲלוּקָה בְּאוֹהָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן that began before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from טומאת מת to כלי חרס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The severe case has a special feature, being divided in tents, that the mild case lacks. That feature explains why the partition works there.

steps.title: This fits the רבנן, but what about רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fits the רבנן, who say the partition does not help in an earthenware vessel. But רבי אליעזר says it does help, so how does he fit the principle?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works well for the רבנן. But what can we say according to רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it has been using. It works for the רבנן but seems to clash with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divided oven was brought as an example of 'something does not affect what is not its kind.' The רבנן, who say the partition does nothing, fit that idea. רבי אליעזר lets the partition work, so he seems to reject the principle.

keyTerms.meaning: that works out fine
what can be said? (a sign of a difficulty)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the Rabbis;
according to Rabbi Eliezer, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח לְרַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the source just completed supports the principle according to both opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the divided oven case as support for the principle that something does not affect what is not its kind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר lets the partition work in the vessel, which seems to go against the principle.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר relies on his קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר agrees with the principle. He rules differently only because his קל וחומר pushes past it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר was saying a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר does not reject the principle. His ruling comes from his קל וחומר from טומאת מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the קל וחומר, רבי אליעזר would also say the partition does nothing in a כלי חרס. A קל וחומר is strong enough to override the general rule. So רבי אליעזר does not contradict the principle; the קל וחומר is an exception to it.

keyTerms.meaning: a logical argument: if a rule holds in the stricter case, it surely holds in the lighter one
he is saying

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer is stating an a fortiori argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that a separate reason, the קל וחומר, overrides the principle in רבי אליעזר's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the principle that something does not affect what is not its kind.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר accepts the principle. His קל וחומר is what makes the partition work.

steps.title: Then use a קל וחומר for a חטאת slaughtered for חולין too
steps.stepSummary: If a קל וחומר can override the principle, we should use one for a חטאת slaughtered for חולין. Slaughtering it for another offering ruins it, so slaughtering it for חולין should ruin it even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there too let us say a קל וחומר: if offerings ruin offerings, then surely חולין should ruin them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If a קל וחומר beats the principle, it should also apply to the case of a חטאת slaughtered for חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said a חטאת slaughtered for חולין stays כשר, because חולין are not the same kind as קדשים. But a חטאת slaughtered for a different offering is פסול. So a קל וחומר seems to follow: if a holy purpose can disqualify it, a non-holy purpose should surely disqualify it.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
sacrificial offerings
profane or disqualify
ordinary, non-sacred food
all the more so

steps.whyThisMatters: This puts at risk the ruling that a חטאת slaughtered for חולין stays כשר. The גמרא now has to explain why the קל וחומר does not apply here.

phrases.english: If so,
there too let us say an a fortiori argument:
phrases.notes: 'There' is the חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין, which was ruled כשר earlier.

phrases.english: If offerings profane offerings,
phrases.notes: Slaughtering a חטאת for the sake of a different offering makes it פסול.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so with non-sacred food?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הָתָם נָמֵי לֵימָא קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer from step 3, that a קל וחומר overrides the principle, and turns it against the ruling about the חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of חולין is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from 'offerings disqualify offerings' would show that חולין should disqualify it even more. Step 3 said a קל וחומר overrides the principle.

steps.title: רב's ruling comes from a verse, not from the principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4. רב's ruling that a חטאת slaughtered for חולין is still kosher does not depend on the earlier principle. It comes from a פסוק, as explained by רבי אלעזר: only intent for another offering ruins an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב's reason follows רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: What is רב's reason? The פסוק says "They shall not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, which they set apart to ה׳." Holy intentions ruin holy things, but non-holy intentions do not ruin holy things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4. It says רב's ruling comes from a פסוק, so no קל וחומר can change it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the challenge was that a קל וחומר should make a חטאת slaughtered for חולין פסול. Now the גמרא says רב learns from the פסוק that only a thought about another offering (קדשים) ruins a קרבן, while a thought about חולין does not. A פסוק beats a קל וחומר, so רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason or source behind a ruling
They will desecrate, meaning make something lose its holy status
Holy things, meaning offerings. Here it also means a thought about an offering.
Non-holy, ordinary. Here it means a thought about ordinary meat.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread the line to mean ordinary things can never affect a קרבן. It is narrower than that: only a wrong thought about another offering ruins it, and a thought about חולין does not.

phrases.english: Rather, the reason of Rav is like Rabbi Elazar;
for Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the reason of Rav?
"And they shall not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel,
which they set apart unto ה׳"
holy things desecrate holy things,
phrases.notes: He means a thought about another offering is what ruins an offering.

phrases.english: but non-holy things do not desecrate holy things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by giving רב's ruling a source in a פסוק instead of the principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new source: a פסוק, which cannot be overridden by a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling depends on the principle, so a קל וחומר could override it and make the חטאת פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב learns from ״וְלֹא יְחַלְּלוּ״ that only intent for another offering ruins an offering. The פסוק blocks the קל וחומר.

steps.title: Then let the word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ block רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: If a פסוק can block a קל וחומר, then the word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ in the פסוק about earthenware vessels should block רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר about the partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that a פסוק can come and override a קל וחומר. Here too, let the word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ come and override רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer it just gave to raise a new challenge against רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that a פסוק defeats a קל וחומר. The word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ seems to say that anything inside the vessel becomes טמא, even with a partition. If so, this פסוק should defeat רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר, which said the partition protects.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see, apparently
Took it out, overrode it
Its interior. This word comes from the פסוק about earthenware vessels becoming טמא.

phrases.english: So we see that a verse comes
and takes it out of a kal vachomer;
here too, let "its interior" come
phrases.notes: This is the word from ויקרא 11:33, the פסוק about a שרץ falling into an earthenware vessel.

phrases.english: and take it out of the kal vachomer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אֲתָא קְרָא אַפְּקֵיהּ מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule from step 5, that a פסוק overrides a קל וחומר, and turns it against רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a partition protects food in an earthenware oven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק beats a קל וחומר. ״תּוֹכוֹ״ seems to teach that a partition does not help, so it should override רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר.

steps.title: 'Its interior' is needed for food sealed in clay
steps.stepSummary: The word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ does not teach anything about partitions. It teaches that food sealed inside clay still becomes טמא when it is placed in the airspace of a טמא oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ is needed for food that someone sealed in clay and put into the airspace of an oven. You might have thought that since the food cannot become טמא by touch, it also cannot become טמא in the oven's airspace. So the פסוק teaches us that it does become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אליעזר. It says ״תּוֹכוֹ״ is used for a different law, so it cannot block his קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clay coating would stop the food from becoming טמא through touch. One might think it is also protected inside the oven. ״תּוֹכוֹ״ teaches that anything in the vessel's airspace becomes טמא regardless. Since the word is used up on this law, it says nothing against partitions.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, meaning the word is used to teach a different law
Kneaded them in clay, meaning sealed them inside clay
Airspace, the empty space inside a vessel
Touching, contact
It would enter your mind, meaning you might have thought
It teaches us, meaning the פסוק tells us otherwise

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being in the airspace of a טמא earthenware vessel is enough to make food טמא, even when the food is shielded from any touching.

phrases.english: This "its interior" is needed
for food that one kneaded in clay,
and put them into the airspace of an oven.
It would enter your mind to say:
since by touching it does not become impure,
phrases.notes: The clay sits between the food and the טמא thing, so the food never really touches it.

phrases.english: in its airspace too they should not become impure
[so it teaches us that they do].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording to finish the thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing the word ״תּוֹכוֹ״ is used for another law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed elsewhere, so it cannot be used to block the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Food sealed in clay cannot become טמא by touch, so it should also stay טהור inside a טמא oven.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״תּוֹכוֹ״ teaches that the food becomes טמא through the oven's airspace, so the word teaches nothing about partitions.

steps.title: The רבנן don't need a פסוק for the clay case
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״תּוֹכוֹ״ to teach that a partition does not help. So how do they know the law of food sealed in clay? The answer: that law is obvious and needs no פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, where do they learn the clay case? These cases do not need a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question and answers it right away. The רבנן do not need ״תּוֹכוֹ״ for the clay case, because that law is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבנן use ״תּוֹכוֹ״ to teach that a partition does not help, the clay case seems to be left without a source. The גמרא answers that food in clay is just like any other food in a טמא oven, so no פסוק is needed. This explains why the רבנן and רבי אליעזר read ״תּוֹכוֹ״ differently.

keyTerms.meaning: These, meaning the cases just mentioned
They do not need a פסוק, because the law is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר uses ״תּוֹכוֹ״ for food sealed in clay, so his קל וחומר about the partition still works. The רבנן say the clay case is obvious, so they are free to use ״תּוֹכוֹ״ to teach that a partition does not help.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: the רבנן use ״תּוֹכוֹ״ for the partition law, so how do they know the clay law?

phrases.english: These do not need a verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the gap left by step 7 for the רבנן's side of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The law is obvious, so it needs no source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״תּוֹכוֹ״, the רבנן would have no source for the clay case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food sealed in clay is treated like any food in a טמא oven, so no פסוק is needed. This leaves the רבנן free to use ״תּוֹכוֹ״ for the partition law.

steps.title: רב יוסף בר אמי sets up a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר אמי announces that he will set two rulings of רב against each other, שינוי קודש against שינוי בעלים, and that he will also resolve the clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר אמי pointed out a contradiction between רב's ruling about changing the offering and רב's ruling about changing the owner, and then he resolved it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line that opens a new topic. The גמרא tells us that רב יוסף בר אמי is about to compare two rulings of רב and show that they seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שינוי קודש means slaughtering an offering with intent for a different kind of offering. שינוי בעלים means slaughtering it with intent for a different owner. The details of the contradiction and the answer come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction (literally 'throws' two sources against each other)
Changing the offering: slaughtering it with intent for a different offering
Changing the owner: slaughtering it with intent for someone other than its owner
And he resolves it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Ami raises a contradiction
between changing the offering and changing the owner,
and he resolves it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר אַמֵּי רָמֵי שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ אַשִּׁינּוּי בְּעָלִים, וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of ״תּוֹכוֹ״ and the partition in steps 6-8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two rulings of רב, one about שינוי קודש and one about שינוי בעלים, seem to contradict each other, and רב יוסף בר אמי will resolve them.

steps.title: רב's first ruling: changing the offering
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת is kosher, but a חטאת slaughtered for an עולה is פסולה. This suggests that only a 'different kind' of intent ruins the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of another חטאת is kosher, but one slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is not? That would mean a different kind of intent ruins it and a similar kind of intent does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first side of the contradiction. It is רב's ruling about changing the offering, and the גמרא draws a rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Intent for another חטאת is 'its own kind', and it does no harm. Intent for an עולה is 'not its kind', and it ruins the offering. So the rule seems to be: different ruins, similar does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, a different type of offering from a חטאת
Apparently / this shows that
Its own kind (similar to it)
Ruins / destroys (makes the offering פסול)

phrases.english: Did Rav say:
A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering is fit,
phrases.notes: He means a different חטאת, such as one the owner owes for another sin.

phrases.english: but for the sake of a burnt offering it is unfit;
apparently, intent that is not of its kind ruins it,
while intent that is of its kind does not ruin it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the contradiction announced in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שינוי קודש, a 'different kind' of intent (an עולה) ruins the חטאת, while a 'same kind' of intent (another חטאת) does not.

steps.title: רב's second ruling: changing the owner points the other way
steps.stepSummary: רב also rules that a חטאת slaughtered for a person who owes a חטאת is פסולה, but one slaughtered for a person who owes an עולה is kosher. This suggests that the 'same kind' of intent ruins it. That is the opposite of step 10.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב said that a חטאת slaughtered for someone who owes a חטאת is פסולה, while one slaughtered for someone who owes an עולה is kosher. That would mean a similar kind of intent ruins it and a different kind does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב's second ruling, about changing the owner, and shows that it leads to the opposite rule from the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'similar' person, someone who also owes a חטאת, ruins the offering. The 'different' person, someone who owes an עולה, does not. In the owner case 'similar' ruins, but in the offering case 'different' ruins, so רב seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a clashing source)
Obligated / owes (an offering)
Of its kind (similar to it)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
A sin offering that one slaughtered
for a person who owes a sin offering is unfit,
but for a person who owes a burnt offering it is fit;
apparently, intent that is of its kind ruins it,
while intent that is not of its kind does not ruin it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רב's owner ruling against his offering ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule drawn from רב's שינוי קודש ruling: only a 'different kind' of intent ruins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב's שינוי בעלים ruling, a 'same kind' of intent ruins and a 'different kind' does not. That is the reverse pattern, so the two rulings seem inconsistent.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In step 10 the change is the type of offering (חטאת or עולה). In step 11 the offering stays a חטאת, and the change is which person it is slaughtered for.

steps.title: Resolving the offering case from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר אמי explains the first case. The Torah says 'slaughter it for a חטאת', and a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת was still slaughtered 'for a חטאת', so it stays kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answers: there, in the offering case, the Torah says 'and slaughter it for a חטאת'. Here a חטאת was slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת, so it fits the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף בר אמי begins to resolve the contradiction. He explains why intent for another חטאת does not ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern in step 10 is not a general rule that 'similar' intent never ruins. It comes from the wording of the פסוק. The Torah only requires that it be slaughtered 'for a חטאת', and intent for another חטאת still meets that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other case)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
And here / and indeed

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the result in the offering case is a matter of how the פסוק is worded, not a general rule about 'similar' and 'different' intent. That removes the basis for the contradiction.

phrases.english: And he resolves it:
There, "And slaughter it for a sin offering"
phrases.notes: ״הָתָם״ is the case of changing the offering. The פסוק is ויקרא 4:33.

phrases.english: is what the Merciful One said,
and here a sin offering was slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: הָתָם ״וְשָׁחַט אֹתָהּ לְחַטָּאת״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11 by explaining the offering ruling from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based distinction: the offering-change ruling depends on the wording of the פסוק, not on a general 'similar or different' rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's two rulings follow opposite general rules about whether 'similar' or 'different' intent ruins an offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the offering case, the פסוק only demands slaughter 'for a חטאת'. Intent for another חטאת meets that, so the offering is kosher.

steps.title: Why a חטאת slaughtered for a person who owes a חטאת is ruined
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו״ means 'for him and not for his fellow.' That 'fellow' is someone like him, who also owes a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here the Torah writes 'and he shall atone for him.' That means for him and not for his fellow. And 'his fellow' means someone similar to him, who owes the same kind of atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף בר אמי now explains רב's second ruling, about slaughtering for another person (שינוי בעלים). This completes his answer to the contradiction from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״עָלָיו״ exclude 'his fellow.' The 'fellow' being excluded is someone like the owner, meaning a person who also owes a חטאת. So intent for a person who owes a חטאת ruins the offering, while intent for a person who owes only an עולה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall atone for him': the פסוק about the owner of a חטאת
His fellow: a person other than the owner
Similar to him
Atonement

steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings of רב come from פסוקים. ״לְחַטָּאת״ lets a חטאת stay kosher when it is slaughtered for another חטאת. ״עָלָיו״ ruins it when it is slaughtered for a person who owes the same kind of atonement.

phrases.english: Here, 'and he shall atone for him' is written:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:26. 'Here' means the case of slaughtering for a different person.

phrases.english: for him, and not for his fellow;
his fellow is similar to him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part resolution begun in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each ruling has its own separate פסוק source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's two rulings seem to follow opposite logic
steps.terutzMaskana: ״עָלָיו״ excludes only a 'fellow' who owes the same kind of atonement, so the two rulings do not clash

steps.title: רב חביבא announces a new contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא will set רב's ruling on שינוי בעלים against the ברייתא of ״תוך תוכו״, and he will also resolve the clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא sets the law of a change of owner against the law of 'the interior of its interior,' and he resolves the contradiction.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that a new contradiction is coming, and the next steps lay it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same pattern as רב יוסף בר אמי in step 9. This time, one side of the clash is a law of טומאה from earlier in the סוגיא: a vessel placed inside a clay vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets two sources against each other
Slaughtering with intent for a different owner
The interior of its interior: a vessel inside a clay vessel
And he resolves it

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva raises a contradiction
between change of owner and 'the interior of its interior,'
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from earlier about a vessel sitting inside a clay vessel.

phrases.english: and resolves it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲבִיבָא רָמֵי שִׁינּוּי בְּעָלִים אַתּוֹךְ תּוֹכוֹ, וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new contradiction after the first one was resolved
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A contradiction exists between רב on שינוי בעלים and the ברייתא of ״תוך תוכו״, and רב חביבא will resolve it

steps.title: Restating רב: only the same kind of intent ruins a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רב's ruling and draws out its rule: only intent of 'its own kind' ruins a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say that a חטאת slaughtered for a person who owes a חטאת is invalid, but one slaughtered for a person who owes an עולה is valid? That means its own kind ruins it, and something not of its kind does not ruin it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב's ruling from step 11 to set up the first side of רב חביבא's contradiction. The real challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of quoting רב again is the general rule it implies. Same kind ruins it, and a different kind has no effect. That is the rule about to be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently, which shows that
Its own kind
Ruins it

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ruling of רב as in step 11. It is quoted again here for a new purpose, to clash with a law of טומאה.

phrases.english: And did Rav say:
a sin offering that one slaughtered for one who is obligated
[a sin offering – it is invalid,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added to finish the sentence; without them, the line jumps straight to the עולה case.

phrases.english: for one who is obligated] a burnt offering – it is valid;
apparently, its own kind ruins it,
something not its kind does not ruin it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of רב חביבא's contradiction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From רב: only intent of the same kind affects a חטאת, and a different kind has no effect

steps.title: The ברייתא shows that a different kind does have an effect
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of ״תוך תוכו״ says that even a כלי שטף, which is not a clay vessel, protects what is inside it. So something not of its kind does have an effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'its interior' becomes impure, but not the interior of its interior. Even a vessel that is purified by rinsing protects what is inside it!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the challenge itself. A law of טומאה seems to go against the rule just drawn from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי שטף is a different kind of vessel from the clay vessel, yet it still blocks the טומאה from reaching its contents. That suggests 'not its kind' can have an effect, which is the opposite of רב's logic in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel that is purified by rinsing (not a clay vessel)
Protects, keeps the contents from becoming impure

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita:
'its interior' – and not the interior of its interior,
phrases.notes: The clay vessel's inside becomes impure, but a vessel sitting inside it does not.

phrases.english: even a vessel purified by rinsing protects!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule drawn from רב in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from רב that something not of its kind has no effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the law of a clay vessel, a vessel of a different kind (כלי שטף) still blocks טומאה, so a different kind does have an effect

steps.title: The word 'interior' is counted four times in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא begins his answer. The פסוק about a clay vessel says תוכו twice, and the extra 'its' on each one makes four mentions in total. The first mention teaches the basic law, and the second is used for a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he answers: 'its interior' is written four times: interior, its interior, interior, its interior. One is for the basic law itself, and one is for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא starts answering the קשיא by counting the word 'interior' in the פסוק as four separate mentions. He assigns the first two jobs here, and the next step finishes the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'the interior,' but it says 'its interior' each time, so each word counts double. That gives the פסוק four mentions to work with. If each mention has its own job, then the law that a כלי שטף protects is a special rule taught by a word in the פסוק, not a general principle.

keyTerms.meaning: He answers / resolves the contradiction
Interior / its interior: the airspace inside the vessel
For itself: the basic law the word plainly teaches
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places
A clay (earthenware) vessel, which becomes impure through its airspace

steps.confusionAlert: The 'four' is not four separate words written in the פסוק. תוכו appears twice, and each one is read as two (תוך plus the extra 'its'), which makes four.

phrases.english: And he answers: 'its interior' is written four times
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 11:33. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: Interior, its interior, interior, its interior.
One is for the law itself;
phrases.notes: This is the plain lesson: something impure inside a clay vessel's airspace makes the food in there impure.

phrases.english: and one is for a גזירה שוה;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רב חביבא's answer to the קשיא raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based limitation: each mention of 'interior' teaches a separate law, so the כלי שטף rule is special to its פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that something not of its kind can have an effect, which goes against רב's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from extra words in the פסוק, so it does not set a general principle (finished in step 18).

steps.title: The last two mentions teach the limits, including that a כלי שטף protects
steps.stepSummary: The third mention teaches that only a clay vessel's interior passes on impurity, not other vessels. The fourth teaches 'its interior, not the interior of its interior,' so even a כלי שטף placed inside protects its contents.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teaches: the interior of this vessel, and not the interior of another kind. The other teaches: 'its interior' and not the interior of its interior, and even a כלי שטף protects.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא finishes giving each mention of 'interior' its job. The last one is the source for the ברייתא's law that a כלי שטף protects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law that a כלי שטף inside a clay vessel protects its contents comes straight from a special word in the פסוק. That makes it a one-time rule for clay vessels. So it cannot be used against רב, and רב's rule still stands: for a חטאת, only intent of 'its own kind' ruins it.

keyTerms.meaning: The interior of this one (the clay vessel only)
The other one
The interior of its interior: a vessel placed inside the clay vessel
Protects, saving its contents from becoming impure

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of תוך תוכו learns its law from a special extra word in the פסוק, so it is not a general rule. It does not contradict רב's rule that only intent of 'its own kind' ruins a חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא answers a contradiction: a law that comes from a special word in a פסוק is limited to its own topic and cannot be carried over to another area, such as שחיטה.

phrases.english: One teaches: the interior of this one
phrases.notes: 'This one' means the clay vessel. Its airspace passes on impurity, but other vessels pass it on only by touch.

phrases.english: and not the interior of another kind of vessel;
the other teaches: 'its interior,' and not the interior of its interior,
and even a כלי שטף protects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list started in step 17 and completes the answer to the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-source limitation: the כלי שטף rule comes from an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fact that a כלי שטף, a different kind of vessel, protects seemed to prove that something not of its kind has an effect, even for a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is a special teaching for clay vessels only, so רב's rule about a חטאת is not contradicted.
